([[Riverside, California]]) * [[Eleanor Roosevelt High School (California)|Eleanor Roosevelt]]
([[Eastvale, California]]) | college = [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] (2025–2026) | draft_year = 2026 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 10 | draft_team = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | career_start = 2026 | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | highlights = * First-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] ([[2025–26 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|2026]]) * [[Big 12]] All-Freshman Team (2026) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2025 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2025]]) * [[California Mr. Basketball]] (2025) }} '''Brayden Burries''' (born September 18, 2005) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A {{Height|ft=6|in=4}} [[Guard (basketball)|guard]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. ==Early life and high school== Burries grew up in [[San Bernardino, California]] and initially attended [[Riverside Polytechnic High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2024/04/17/all-inland-boys-basketball-roosevelts-brayden-burries-is-the-ie-varsity-player-of-the-year/|title=All-Inland Boys Basketball: Roosevelt’s Brayden Burries is the IE Varsity Player of the Year|first=Eric-Paul|last=Johnson|work=[[The Press-Enterprise]]|date=April 17, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024}} He transferred to [[Eleanor Roosevelt High School (California)|Eleanor Roosevelt High School]] after his freshman season.{{cite web|url=https://www.sbsun.com/2023/11/17/roosevelt-boys-basketball-team-has-the-pieces-for-a-memorable-season/|title=Roosevelt boys basketball team has the pieces for a memorable season|first=Eric-Paul|last=Johnson|work=[[The San Bernardino Sun]]|date=November 17, 2023|access-date=November 7, 2024}} Burries was ineligible to play his sophomore season following the transfer.{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/story/2023-12-28/prep-basketball-brayden-burries-eastvale-roosevelt|title=Brayden Burries helps Eastvale Roosevelt reach Damien semifinals|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=December 28, 2023|access-date=February 5, 2025|last=Sondheimer|first=Eric}} He averaged 24.8 points, 7.9 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.7 steals per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/acc/2024/05/09/duke-basketball-2025-recruiting-class-aj-dybantsa-cameron-boozer/73549010007/|title=Duke basketball recruiting: Blue Devils 2025 players to target|work=[[The Fayetteville Observer]]|date=May 9, 2024|access-date=November 7, 2024}} He was selected to play in the [[2025 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2025/01/27/brayden-burries-grace-knox-and-aliyahna-morris-earn-mcdonalds-all-american-game-nods/|title=Brayden Burries, Grace Knox and Aliyahna Morris earn McDonald’s All-American Game nods|first=Eric-Paul|last=Johnson|work=[[The Press-Enterprise]]|date=January 27, 2025|access-date=January 28, 2025}} Burries was a consensus five-star recruit and one of the top players in the 2025 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/kentucky/men-s-basketball/kentucky-basketball-has-offered-a-five-star-guard-in-the-2025-class|title=Kentucky basketball has offered a five-star guard in the 2025 class|first=Andrew|last=Stefaniak|website=[[SI.com]]|date=July 23, 2024|access-date=November 7, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2025/01/21/brayden-burries-tennessee-basketball-recruiting/77702479007/|title=Five-star Brayden Burries visits Tennessee basketball for Mississippi State game|first=Mike|last=Wilson|work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]|date=January 23, 2025|access-date=February 3, 2025}} Burries accepted an athletic scholarship from the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]].{{Cite web |title=5-star guard Brayden Burries commits to Arizona |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/article/5-star-guard-brayden-burries-commits-to-arizona-246256663/ |access-date=2026-04-03 |website=[[247Sports.com]] |language=en|date=2025-04-10|last=Bossi|first=Eric}} ==College career== Burries scored 32 points in the regular-season finale against [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]]. He was named to the All-[[Big 12]] First Team and Big 12 All-Freshman team, and was a finalist for the [[Jerry West Award]].{{cite web |title=Bradley, Burries Earn All-American Honors |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2026/3/18/mens-basketball-bradley-burries-earn-all-american-honors.aspx |website=[[Arizona Wildcats]] |access-date=April 22, 2026 |date=March 18, 2026}} Burries averaged 16.1 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.5 steals per game as a freshman.{{cite news |last=Parker |first=Derek |title=NBA Draft Scouting Report: Arizona Guard Brayden Burries |url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/nba-draft-scouting-report-arizona-guard-brayden-burries |access-date=April 22, 2026 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=April 20, 2026}} Following the end of the season, Burries opted to enter the [[2026 NBA draft]] on April 24, 2026, making him the second player from Arizona to enter the draft following [[Koa Peat]].{{cite web |title=Brayden Burries makes Arizona fans wait but officially declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/other/brayden-burries-makes-arizona-fans-wait-but-officially-declares-for-nba-draft/ar-AA21FqXH |website=[[MSN]] |access-date=May 13, 2026 |last=Rubenstein|first=Alan|date=May 2026}} ==Professional career== On June 23, 2026, Burries was selected with the tenth overall pick by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49162673|title=Bucks draft Burries, Ament after Giannis trade: 'We're building'|website=espn.com|last=Collier|first=Jamal|date=June 24, 2026|access-date=July 11, 2026}} ==Personal life== Burries is a [[Christianity|Christian]].{{cite web |last=Mattingly |first=Mallory |title=ARIZONA WILDCATS FRESHMAN PRAISES GOD, WIN OR LOSE |url=https://www.movieguide.org/news-articles/arizona-wildcats-freshman-praises-god-no-matter-what.html |access-date=2026-06-28|date=2026-04-07|website=movieguide.org}} Burries's father, Bobby, played college basketball at [[San Bernardino Valley College]] and [[Cal State San Bernardino Coyotes|Cal State San Bernardino]], where he is a member of the school's athletic hall of fame.{{cite web|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2023/09/21/high-school-guard-ranked-no-11-nationally-visits-aztecs/|title=High school guard ranked No. 11 nationally visits Aztecs|work=[[The San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=September 21, 2023|access-date=February 5, 2025|last=Zeigler|first=Mark}} His mother, Hannah, played [[college softball]] at [[Tennessee Lady Volunteers softball|Tennessee]] and basketball at Cal State San Bernardino for one year as a graduate transfer.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/tennessee/article/five-star-guard-brayden-burries-enjoys-great-official-visit-with-tennessee-vols-basketball-rick-barnes-rod-clark-zakai-zeigler-244588527/|title=Five-star guard Brayden Burries enjoys 'great' official visit with Tennessee basketball|first=Ben|last=McKee|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=January 22, 2025|access-date=February 5, 2025}} ==References==
